title: KV cache: make compaction deterministic across TP ranks to prevent divergence/stalls
author: Samir Qureshi
description: Context: We’ve seen intermittent TP hangs under memory pressure that correlate strongly with KV cache compaction activity. Root cause (repro’d in benchmark-lab mixed prefill/decode and in one Dedicated A100 cluster): KV compaction was being triggered based on rank-local allocator state and “best effort” heuristics. Under sustained load, ranks can make different compaction decisions (or compact different blocks) within the same decode step, leading to rank divergence: one rank proceeds to the next step with a different set of KV pages/handles while another rank is still relocating pages or waiting on a different stream dependency. In practice this shows up as a silent stall where one or more ranks block on a collective in the next iteration because a peer is stuck in compaction/copy, or worse, ranks enter different collective sequences due to early-return paths. Change summary: (1) Introduce a TP-synchronized compaction plan: rank0 computes a compact-or-skip decision and a deterministic move plan (block ids + destination ids + epoch), then broadcasts to all ranks before any relocation begins. All ranks execute the same plan or all skip. (2) Make compaction “epoch” explicit and monotonic (kv_compaction_epoch) and attach it to per-request decode steps; early exits/cancellation now still advance through a shared barrier to avoid leaving peers mid-epoch. (3) Ensure stream safety: relocation copies + frees now happen on a dedicated compaction stream, with explicit event handoff to the compute stream before the next decode iteration touches the relocated pages. This removes the previous implicit dependency on allocator-side synchronization (which was not consistent across ranks). (4) Harden against fragmentation edge-cases: if the move plan cannot be satisfied (e.g., insufficient contiguous destination pages after reservation), we fail the compaction attempt consistently across ranks for that epoch and continue without partial moves. (5) Observability: add structured logs and counters for compaction epochs, plan sizes, and “rank plan mismatch” (should remain zero), plus a trace annotation tying compaction epochs to decode step ids. Tests: Add a TP stress regression that forces compaction under decode by lowering KV reserve watermark and injecting fragmentation patterns; validate that (a) all ranks report identical compaction epoch + moved blocks, (b) no stalls/hangs over N iterations, and (c) post-compaction KV reads remain correct. The stress test is gated in CI on a 4-GPU TP runner and is also runnable via benchmark-lab harness. Risk/perf: Compaction now has one additional broadcast per epoch and an extra event sync between compaction and compute streams; microbench impact measured within noise (<0.3% tokens/s) on A100-80GB for our long-context decode profile, and the broadcast is amortized since compaction epochs are infrequent relative to decode iterations. This should substantially reduce stall probability in the pathological fragmentation regime. Rollout: Safe to ship behind existing TP stability flags; no API behavior changes. This is a correctness + reliability fix and is part of the ENG-4821 TP stability initiative.

runtime/kv: execute deterministic move plan on compaction stream w/ event handoff
runtime/kv: make compaction failure consistent across ranks; remove partial move early-return
runtime/tp: plumb rank/world info to KV compaction planner; add mismatch assertions (debug)
tests/tp: add kv_compaction_under_pressure stress scenario + CI gating

conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you clarify why we need both the broadcast plan and the event handoff? I want to make sure we’re not papering over an ordering bug elsewhere.

Samir Qureshi (author): The broadcast fixes decision divergence (whether/what to compact). The event handoff fixes stream visibility (when relocated pages are safe for compute). Previously ranks could agree on compaction but still observe different readiness because relocation ran on different streams with implicit deps. Added a comment in kv_cache_compaction.cc explaining the two failure modes + linked the repro signature from SUP-48377.
Noah Patel (review): Please make the failure path consistent across ranks. Right now if reservation fails mid-plan on one rank, it returns early and peers keep moving blocks. That’s still divergence.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good catch. Updated: reservation happens first, and if it fails we broadcast a compact=false for that epoch (plan_size=0). All ranks skip relocation. Added a test that simulates reservation failure by constraining destination pages.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Do we need a device-wide sync here? I’m worried about introducing perf cliffs with cudaDeviceSynchronize.

Samir Qureshi (author): No device sync. It’s per-stream: record event on compaction stream after relocation, then wait on compute stream before next decode step consumes KV. Verified via Nsight Systems that we don’t serialize unrelated streams.
Sofia Ivanova (review): Scheduler angle: decode loop can be cancelled; are we sure we won’t hold a barrier forever if the request is torn down mid-epoch?

Samir Qureshi (author): Added a cancellation-safe “epoch finalize” that always participates in the rank barrier once compaction is entered. If the request is cancelled, we mark the epoch aborted and proceed to finalize; watchdog/abort semantics are handled elsewhere (ENG-4826). Also added structured log kv_compaction_epoch_state=aborted.
Marcus Reed (review): Stress test looks good. Please add it to the tp_stress_suite YAML with a conservative runtime cap so it’s stable in CI.
Samir Qureshi (author): Done. Capped to 90s, 3 runs, and made fragmentation seed deterministic. Also added a skip if GPUs < 4.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. This aligns with the stall signature we saw in repro notes. Please keep the debug mismatch assertion under a debug-only flag.
Samir Qureshi (author): Ack; mismatch assertion is behind RUNTIME_DEBUG_TP_ASSERTS and logs a counter otherwise.
release_notes: Runtime: Fix KV cache compaction under tensor-parallel load by making compaction decisions deterministic across ranks and adding a TP stress regression test. Reduces risk of rank divergence leading to stalls/timeouts under memory pressure.
